project.name: picotls
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source inspected here is the ARVO workspace checkout at `254a1801ede6ed8f4b0c86303c0a9cb8dab9b40f`; its `lib/minicrypto-pem.c` line map matches the saved ASan trace and it lacks any `last_byte1 < byte_index` rejection before the parameters parse. ARVO metadata separately reports `b1999d666e431cf2879b18076cc4218e5c3dcb74` / `75f9c33cef261046f75c6fe3a02f9912e55211ee` as vulnerable/fixed commits, but local picotls history shows `b1999d6` already adds the missing `last_byte1 < byte_index` guard and is therefore the actual fix for this staged path. The staged `patch.diff` is the later follow-on `75f9c33` hardening change, whose diff context assumes that earlier guard is already present.

bug_description.original: Crash Type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 Crash State: ptls_asn1_read_type ptls_asn1_validation_recursive ptls_asn1_validation_recursive Sanitizer: address (ASAN)
bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta.report.comments[0].content / staged vulnerable source snapshot / saved sanitizer_trace.txt / local picotls history
bug_description.normalized: The staged 259-byte `fuzz-asn1` witness makes the harness set `bytes_max = 0x0100` and copy the next 256 bytes into a temp file. The final byte is `0xff`, so the outer selector at `fuzz-asn1.c:64` becomes `3` and enters the `ret == 2 || ret == 3` file-loading branch, but the later `if (ret == 2)` at line 91 tests the shadowed inner `ret = write(fd, bytes, bytes_max)`, which evaluates to `256`, so control falls through to `ptls_minicrypto_load_private_key`. `ptls_get_pem_object` accepts the `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` prefix line and, using the sparse base64 fragments on the following lines, decodes the logical DER object `30 10 02 01 00 30 00 06 7f 28 84 0a 28 32 8c 07 82 8a`. That object is stored as `pkey->vec` with `len == 18`, but because the PEM buffer starts at capacity 0 and grows through `ptls_buffer_reserve`, its backing heap allocation is 1024 bytes. In `ptls_minicrypto_asn1_decode_private_key`, the outer sequence and version are accepted, the embedded AlgorithmIdentifier sequence is declared as zero-length (`30 00`), and the OID parse still advances `byte_index` from 7 to 8 so `last_byte1 < byte_index`. The staged vulnerable source performs no `last_byte1 < byte_index` rejection before calling `ptls_asn1_validation_recursive(bytes + byte_index, last_byte1 - byte_index, ...)`, so the `size_t` span underflows from `7 - 8` to `SIZE_MAX`. Recursive ASN.1 validation then treats the remaining attacker bytes as a constructed object with forged length `0x0a28328c`, recurses again from original offset 15, and in that nested parse `ptls_asn1_read_length` consumes a second length byte from original offset 18, the first byte past the 18-byte logical DER extent. That out-of-bounds byte becomes the low byte of a nested primitive length, so the child parse returns a consumed span in `[35332, 35587]`; the parent adds that to its own `byte_index = 7`, still satisfies `byte_index < last_byte` against the forged `last_byte = 170406547`, and immediately launches another recursive parse from original offset `35347 + heap_byte`. That pointer is tens of kilobytes past the 1024-byte allocation, so the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow occurs at `ptls_asn1_read_type` line 86 when the next recursion executes `uint8_t first_byte = bytes[0];`.

source.description: First project-code statement on the vulnerability path that consumes attacker-controlled PEM body text and appends decoded DER bytes into the private-key buffer.
source.value_from: In the staged 259-byte `poc`, bytes 0..1 are `01 00`, so the harness writes bytes 2..257 to a 256-byte temp file. Byte 258 is `0xff`; it only selects the outer `ret == 2 || ret == 3` file-loading branch, and the actual private-key call happens because the shadowed `ret = write(fd, bytes, bytes_max)` returns `256` and makes line 91 fall through to line 102. After the accepted `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` line, the surviving base64 fragments on lines 3..9 (`M`, `B`, `AC`, `AQ`, `A`, `wA`, `AZ/KIQKKDKMB4KK`) decode to `30 10 02 01 00 30 00 06 7f 28 84 0a 28 32 8c 07 82 8a`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the decoded object becomes `pkey->vec`: `len` records the logical DER extent `18`, while the backing heap allocation was already grown from capacity 0 to 1024 by the first `ptls_buffer__do_pushv`.

sink.description: After the nested long-form length overread inflates the child return span, the parent recursive loop invokes `ptls_asn1_validation_recursive` again on `bytes + (35339 + heap_byte)` relative to the parameters sub-buffer, i.e. original allocation offset `35347 + heap_byte`. That pointer is far beyond the 1024-byte PEM backing allocation, and the next `ptls_asn1_read_type` immediately dereferences it here, matching the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow.

root_cause.description: The staged vulnerable source gates the parameters parse only on `*decode_error == 0`. It does not reject the already true `last_byte1 < byte_index` condition after OID parsing, so the next step subtracts `last_byte1 - byte_index` as an unsigned span and underflows.

parser_admitted.description: The staged temp file's second line begins with `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----`. `ptls_compare_separator_line` verifies only the prefix components and the trailing five dashes, and does not require end-of-line afterwards, so the appended `0xff` byte and trailing spaces do not prevent the BEGIN line from being accepted.

private_key_loader_selected.description: The final witness byte `0xff` makes the outer selector at line 64 evaluate to `3`, so execution enters the `ret == 2 || ret == 3` file-loading branch. Inside that branch, `int fd, ret;` shadows the selector, `ret = write(fd, bytes, bytes_max)` stores `256`, and this `if (ret == 2)` predicate is therefore false, so control falls through to the private-key loader call at line 102.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness interprets the first two witness bytes as a 256-byte temp-file length, copies bytes 2..257 into that file, uses final byte `0xff` to enter the `ret == 2 || ret == 3` file-loading branch, then falls through to `ptls_minicrypto_load_private_key` because the shadowed inner `ret = write(...)` stores `256` and makes `if (ret == 2)` false.
PEM parsing accepts the `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY` prefix line, base64-decodes sparse body fragments into an 18-byte DER object, and stores it as `pkey->vec` with a 1024-byte backing allocation.

PKCS#8 parsing accepts the outer sequence and version, parses a zero-length inner AlgorithmIdentifier sequence, then lets OID parsing advance past `last_byte1` and enters the parameters parse without any `last_byte1 < byte_index` rejection.

The underflowed parameters span makes recursive ASN.1 validation treat the remaining bytes as a huge constructed object, recurse again from original offset 15, overread the next length byte past the 18-byte DER extent, convert that byte into a huge returned span, and then iterate once more into `ptls_asn1_read_type` on a pointer far past the 1024-byte allocation, matching the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: The witness starts with `01 00`, so the harness sets `bytes_max = 256`, allocates `bytes`, and copies witness bytes 2..257 into that buffer as the future temp-file contents. After this loop, the only unread witness byte is the final selector byte at offset 258.
The remaining witness byte is `0xff`, so the outer selector becomes `3` and execution enters the `ret == 2 || ret == 3` file-loading branch instead of the standalone ASN.1 helper branches.
Inside that branch, `int fd, ret;` shadows the outer selector. `write(fd, bytes, 256)` stores the temp file and returns `256`, so the short-write early exit is not taken.
The later predicate uses the shadowed inner `ret`, not the selector byte. Because step 3 set `ret = 256`, `if (ret == 2)` is false and control falls through to `ptls_minicrypto_load_private_key`.

After the accepted `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY` prefix line, each `fgets` buffer is decoded as a C string, so embedded `\0` bytes terminate the visible line prefix and only the surviving base64 fragments `M`, `B`, `AC`, `AQ`, `A`, `wA`, and `AZ/KIQKKDKMB4KK` contribute. Together they decode into the exact 18-byte DER sequence `30 10 02 01 00 30 00 06 7f 28 84 0a 28 32 8c 07 82 8a`.

The decoded object is published as `pkey->vec` with logical length `18`. Because `ptls_buffer_init(&buf, "", 0)` started at capacity 0 and the first `ptls_buffer_reserve` rounds growth up to 1024, those 18 logical DER bytes reside in a 1024-byte heap allocation.

fine_trace.code:
byte_index = ptls_asn1_get_expected_type_and_length(bytes, bytes_max, byte_index, 0x30, &seq0_length, NULL, &last_byte0,
                                                        decode_error, log_ctx);
fine_trace.note: The DER begins with `30 10`, so outer PKCS#8 sequence parsing sets `byte_index = 2` and `last_byte0 = 18`, matching the logical `pkey->vec.len` extent.
The next three DER bytes are `02 01 00`, so the version INTEGER is accepted and the cursor advances from offset 2 to offset 5.

fine_trace.code:
byte_index = ptls_asn1_get_expected_type_and_length(bytes, bytes_max, byte_index, 0x30, &seq1_length, NULL, &last_byte1,
                                                            decode_error, log_ctx);
fine_trace.note: At offsets 5..6 the bytes are `30 00`, so the embedded AlgorithmIdentifier sequence is parsed as zero-length. The returned cursor is `byte_index = 7`, and the declared end of that inner sequence is also `last_byte1 = 7`.

Despite the zero-length inner sequence, this call still reads `bytes[7] == 0x06` as an OID tag. Because it was invoked with `bytes_max = last_byte1 = 7`, there is no room for a length byte, so `oid_length` stays `0` while `byte_index` advances to `8`, leaving `last_byte1 < byte_index`.

Control still enters the parameters block because the staged vulnerable source checks only `*decode_error == 0`. Unlike local commit `b1999d6`, there is no `if (last_byte1 < byte_index)` rejection here, even though step 10 already established that the cursor has passed the declared end of the inner sequence.

The parameters parse subtracts `last_byte1 - byte_index` as unsigned `size_t`: `7 - 8` wraps to `SIZE_MAX`. Recursive validation is therefore invoked at original DER offset 8 with an effectively unbounded length.

fine_trace.code:
byte_index =
    ptls_asn1_read_length(bytes, bytes_max, byte_index, &length, &indefinite_length, &last_byte, decode_error, level, log_ctx);
fine_trace.note: Starting at original DER offset 8, `ptls_asn1_read_type` first interprets `7f 28` as a constructed high-tag-number object, and this `ptls_asn1_read_length` then parses `84 0a 28 32 8c` as long-form length `0x0a28328c`. That sets `last_byte = 170406547` even though only 10 logical DER bytes remain from offset 8 onward.

fine_trace.code:
byte_index += ptls_asn1_validation_recursive(bytes + byte_index, last_byte - byte_index, decode_error,
                                                                 level + 1, log_ctx);
fine_trace.note: Because the first parameters object is constructed and `byte_index < last_byte`, the validator recurses again from original DER offset 15 with `bytes_max = 170406540`, carrying the underflowed extent deeper into the parse.

In that nested parse, tag `0x07` is treated as primitive and `0x82` at original DER offset 16 claims a two-byte long-form length. The first length byte comes from original offset 17 (`0x8a`); this second load reads original offset 18, which is the first byte past `pkey->vec.len == 18`. That out-of-bounds byte is not source-grounded, but because it is a single byte the resulting nested `length` is necessarily `0x8a00 | heap_byte` and the nested `last_byte` becomes `35332 + heap_byte`.

fine_trace.code:
ptls_asn1_dump_content(bytes, last_byte, byte_index, log_ctx);
byte_index = last_byte;
fine_trace.note: This crashing path passes `log_ctx == NULL`, so the dump helper does nothing and the primitive child returns `byte_index = last_byte = 35332 + heap_byte` to its caller.

The parent constructed-object frame was at original offset 8 with local `byte_index = 7` and forged `last_byte = 170406547`. After adding the child return from step 16, its `byte_index` becomes `35339 + heap_byte`, which is still below the forged `last_byte`, so the loop immediately schedules another recursive parse from `bytes + byte_index`.

That next recursion starts at original allocation offset `8 + (35339 + heap_byte) = 35347 + heap_byte`. Even the minimum case is far past the 1024-byte PEM backing allocation, so the first dereference in `ptls_asn1_read_type` becomes the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. Fine-trace steps 15-18 close the same recursive descent as the saved ASan stack and end at `ptls_asn1_read_type` line 86, the reported heap-buffer-overflow read.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes at exact reviewed project frames. The saved stack `ptls_asn1_read_type -> ptls_asn1_validation_recursive -> ptls_asn1_validation_recursive -> ptls_minicrypto_asn1_decode_private_key` matches fine-trace steps 18 -> 17/14 -> 12, and the harness frame at `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` line 102 matches step 4's fallthrough into `ptls_minicrypto_load_private_key`.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` is follow-on commit `75f9c33cef261046f75c6fe3a02f9912e55211ee`, which only changes an already-present `if (last_byte1 < byte_index)` check to `if (*decode_error == 0 && last_byte1 < byte_index)`. The exact staged vulnerable source at workspace HEAD `254a1801ede6ed8f4b0c86303c0a9cb8dab9b40f` lacks that guard entirely. Local history shows commit `b1999d666e431cf2879b18076cc4218e5c3dcb74` adds the missing `last_byte1 < byte_index` rejection and is the actual source-level fix for this path.

format.name: fuzz-asn1 feeder input
format.contract: Exactly the staged 259-byte witness: bytes 0..1 are `01 00`, so the harness allocates and later writes a 256-byte temp file; bytes 2..257 are that temp file, whose second line begins `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` and whose accepted base64 body decodes to `30 10 02 01 00 30 00 06 7f 28 84 0a 28 32 8c 07 82 8a`; byte 258 is `0xff`, so the outer selector at line 64 becomes `3` and enters the file-loading branch, and because the shadowed inner `ret = write(fd, bytes, bytes_max)` returns `256`, line 91's `if (ret == 2)` is false and line 102 calls `ptls_minicrypto_load_private_key`.
